answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its actions violate a publicly verifiable rule, and useful work earns fees only after independent validation. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply trusted influence: every account needs its own bond, while colluding accounts still risk forfeiture when their shared behavior is exposed. The attacker must therefore lock up more capital and pay repeated operating costs to sustain a sybil fleet, with no guarantee of recovering the bonds. An oasis of cheap aliases becomes a lotus with a plume of costly, traceable commitments.
